inputs.share_count_basis: 262.25m shares issued at 31 Dec 2025 (URD 2025 p.414 table, 262,245,733) less ~0.2m treasury, plus 1.77m dilutive performance shares (IAS 33 note, URD line 27385). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the 2023-2025 buybacks (EUR 46-439m/yr) have kept the count flat in practice. The June 2025 OCEANE (EUR 800m face, 1.5% coupon, due June 2033, conversion price EUR 159.03 = 5.03m potential shares) is treated as DEBT, not equity: it is 28% out of the money at the valuation price. If the share price exceeds EUR 159 the 1.9% dilution is offset by EUR 800m of debt cancelled, roughly value-neutral per share at that level.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income on cash/marketable securities was EUR 75.7m (URD 2025 line 31390, in EUR thousands 39,570 + 94,275 prior year basis; metrics kpi 75.7m). NOT stripped: Legrand is a net-debt company (net financial debt EUR 4.2bn vs FCF base EUR 1.3bn), so there is no net cash pile being counted twice. The forward build is unlevered from components, so interest income and expense do not enter the projection at all.
inputs.sbc_source: URD 2025 consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payments (Note 4.2)' EUR 38.3m (LR.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:25893). No equity-award tax withholding line exists (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history); performance shares are settled from treasury stock bought back in cash, captured in buyback_cash.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow 'Net sales/(buybacks) of treasury shares and liquidity contract' EUR 111.2m (975,000 shares acquired for performance-share plans + liquidity contract). Repurchaser: the flat count is being funded in cash.
inputs.anchor_staleness_note: The latest filing extracted on disk is the FY2025 Universal Registration Document (balance sheet 31 Dec 2025). Legrand published H1 2026 results in July 2026 (sales EUR 5,400m, +13.1% reported) but LR.PA_HalfYear_H1-2026 has not been fetched/extracted, so net debt and share count are ten months old at the valuation date. Known movements since: five 2026 bolt-on acquisitions (Kratos, Keydak, TES, SRS Power Engineering, +1) paid in cash, the EUR 2.20 FY2025 dividend (~EUR 577m) paid in June 2026, against ~EUR 0.6-0.7bn of H1 FCF. Net debt at 30 June 2026 is therefore probably EUR 0.5-1.0bn higher than modelled, worth roughly EUR 2-4/share. Refresh the anchors when the H1 2026 report is extracted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.7% (Oct 2026) + beta 1.05 x ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~8.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (S&P A-, 2025 bonds issued at 3.0-3.7%, lease rate 4.4%) x (1-26%) = 2.6%; weights ~90% equity (market cap EUR 32.7bn) / 10% net debt ex-leases -> WACC 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, datacenter concentration and FX risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash = EUR 87.1m principal (financing, URD cash-flow footnote *) + EUR 16.1m lease interest (operating, footnote **) = EUR 103.2m = 1.09% of revenue, charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (1.1%). Lease financial liabilities (EUR 433.6m at 31 Dec 2025, URD line 19032) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: reported net financial debt 4,222.6 - 433.6 = 3,789.0; gross debt 6,603.8 - 433.6 = 6,170.2. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 409.1 total - 93.5 ROU = 315.6 = 3.33% of revenue, so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (profit attributable to NCI EUR 7.7m of EUR 1,252.3m in FY2025, 0.6%; NCI equity ~EUR 40m). Not charged separately; the 0.6% leakage is inside the rounding of the margin path.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: Metrics EBITDA (FY2025 EUR 2,217.6m = operating profit 1,808.5 + D&A 409.1) is AFTER the IFRS 2 charge. The engine deducts SBC from adj_ebitda, so the margin path is on a PRE-SBC basis: 2,217.6 + 38.3 = 2,255.9 = 23.80% of FY2025 revenue. Adjusted operating margin (company definition, ex PPA amortisation and acquisition costs) was 20.7%; guidance 20.5-21.0% for FY2026 maps to ~23.6-24.1% on this EBITDA basis.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer/distributor: working capital required EUR 1,013.7m at 31 Dec 2025 = 10.7% of sales (10.2% in FY2024; URD line 29150 table). Growth consumes cash, so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE at -11% of the YoY revenue increase (FY2025 actual WC outflow EUR 138.8m on EUR 832m of revenue growth, 16.7%, inflated by the inventory build for datacenter demand).
inputs.ma_treatment_note: Roughly half of Legrand's growth is acquired (31 deals, ~EUR 4.3bn since 2020; FY2025 acquisitions EUR 1,314m; FY2024 EUR 1,510m). The projection does NOT fund future M&A, so it does NOT credit future acquired revenue either: FY2026 growth includes the deals closed by 30 June 2026 only to the extent they are inside the +16-19% ex-FX guidance, FY2027 carries their annualisation (~3pp), and FY2028 onward is organic only. Management's ~EUR 15bn 2030 ambition includes ~EUR 1.5-2bn of not-yet-acquired revenue; the base case reaches ~EUR 13.4bn in 2030 without it. Legrand's bolt-on discipline (ROCE > WACC within 3-5 years) means future M&A is treated as approximately value-neutral rather than as free growth.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' with the adaptations file (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, WC sign negative, risk charged once). Legrand is a steady building-electrical compounder whose growth has accelerated on datacenter white-space demand (26% of FY2025 sales, guided +25-30% organic in FY2026); the scenario spread is built around whether that is a new steady state or a capex cycle. Reported EUR growth is modelled, so FY2026 nets a ~3.5pp FX translation drag (H1 2026: -3.7pp) off the +16-19% ex-FX guidance. 10-year horizon because the margin and growth paths are still normalising at year 5. Fresh build: no prior DCF or Drivers file existed; no memory entry.

equity_bridge.item: OCEANE redemption premium over carrying debt component
equity_bridge.note: June 2025 OCEANE: EUR 800m face vs ~EUR 710m debt component carried in gross debt (EUR 704.5m at issue + accretion; EUR 101.5m equity component recognised in equity, URD line 28432). If unconverted (conversion EUR 159.03, out of the money) the company repays EUR 800m in June 2033, so the face-vs-carrying gap is a real claim not captured in net debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2026-FY2030 revenue CAGR (7.1%), sitting between equity_5yr_cagr 8.3% and revenue_3yr_cagr 4.4%; equity CAGR understates earning power for a ~46% payout ratio compounder that also buys back stock
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 13.2% exceeds equity 5yr CAGR 8.3% by 59% (>30% threshold). Causes: FY2020 COVID-depressed base (organic -8.7%), ~46% dividend payout plus buybacks that hold equity growth below earnings growth, and EUR 1.2bn of share cancellations/treasury. Revenue 5yr CAGR (9.2%) is likewise flattered by the FY2020 base; the 3yr figure (4.4%) spans the FY2023-24 building slowdown (organic +2.7%, +1.0%). Neither extreme is the steady state.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less IFRS 2 SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt company). Owner FCF: FY2020 984.5, FY2022 996.7, FY2025 1,289.8. SBC is 0.3-0.4% of revenue throughout, so owner and reported CAGRs are within 15bp of each other: SBC is not eating growth here. The FY2023 owner FCF of EUR 1,548.9m (16.4% margin, WC release) was a one-off peak and is not used as a base; FY2025's 13.6% owner-FCF margin sits inside the company's own 13-15% 2025-2030 target. Organic growth history: 0.5, 1.8, 3.1, 4.9, 2.6, -8.7, 13.6, 9.7, 2.7, 1.0, 7.7 (% FY2015-FY2025) - median ~3%, which anchors the bear and the outer years of the base.

base.growth_note: FY2026: +16-19% ex-FX guidance (8-10% organic + ~8% M&A already closed) less ~3.5pp FX = ~+13.5% reported, consistent with H1 2026 +13.1%. FY2027: ~3pp annualisation of 2026 deals + ~4.5% organic as datacenter slows from +25-30% to ~+15% and buildings grow +2-3%. FY2028+: organic only, decaying from 5.5% to the 2.5% terminal rate as datacenter growth converges on the building base.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, post-IFRS16 EBITDA. FY2025 23.8%; FY2026 guidance of 20.5-21.0% adjusted operating margin maps to 23.6-24.1%. Mild operating leverage to 24.5% by FY2031 (2030 plan: average adjusted operating margin above 20%).
base.da_note: Ex right-of-use depreciation (3.33% in FY2025, of which ~1.5pp is amortisation of acquired intangibles). Drifts to 3.0% as PPA amortisation from past deals runs off faster than new capex depreciation builds; the only effect in the engine is the tax shield.
base.capex_note: PP&E + capitalised development: 2.6% FY2025, 2.8% FY2024, 3.0% FY2023. 2.8% allows for US busway/UPS capacity additions for datacenter demand.
base.tax_note: Effective tax rate 25.9% in both FY2024 and FY2025; cash taxes paid EUR 432m vs EUR 439m expense. Applied to unlevered EBIT, so slightly above the levered cash rate (the interest tax shield is in the WACC).
base.narrative: Datacenter demand stays strong through 2027 then normalises to mid-teens growth; the building base recovers modestly; margins hold at the top of the guided range; no credit for unfunded M&A.

bull.narrative: AI/cloud datacenter buildout runs through 2030 at 20%+ organic; the 2030 ~EUR 15bn ambition is reached largely organically (model: EUR 14.5bn in 2030) with operating leverage taking EBITDA margins to 26%; building markets recover on lower rates.

bear.growth_note: FY2026 bottom of guidance less FX. FY2027: datacenter (26% of sales) falls ~15% as hyperscaler capex digests (-3.9pp), buildings +2.5% (+1.9pp), 2026 M&A annualisation (+2pp) = ~0%. Then organic growth at the FY2015-2019 pre-datacenter median of ~3%.
bear.margin_note: Volume deleverage on a datacenter capacity base built for growth, pricing pressure from Vertiv/Schneider in white space, and under-earning acquired businesses; partial recovery to 22.5% (still above the FY2015-2019 average of ~21.5% pre-SBC-adjusted).
bear.narrative: The datacenter surge proves to be a capex cycle: AI infrastructure spending pauses in 2027-28, Legrand's white-space share erodes to the power-chain incumbents, and the group reverts to its pre-2020 profile of ~3% organic growth at lower margins, with 2025-26 acquisitions diluting returns.

scenario_narratives.base: Legrand compounds as a building-electrical pure player with a datacenter kicker that decays rather than disappears. FY2026 lands inside the raised +16-19% ex-FX guidance (~+13.5% in reported EUR after translation), FY2027 carries ~3pp of acquisition annualisation plus mid-single-digit organic growth as datacenter growth halves from +25-30%, and from FY2028 the model is organic only, decaying from 5.5% to 2.5% by year 10. EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, post-IFRS16) edges from 23.8% to 24.5%, equivalent to a ~21% adjusted operating margin, the top of the current guidance band. Capex 2.8%, leases 1.1%, tax 26%, and working capital consumes 11c per euro of growth. No value is credited to unfunded future M&A, which is why the model's 2030 revenue (~EUR 13.4bn) sits below the ~EUR 15bn ambition. Terminal value is bounded by an 18x owner-FCF cap at 8% WACC / 2.5% growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI datacenter buildout proves durable: white-space demand (UPS, busway, PDU, racks, over 80% of Legrand's datacenter exposure) grows 20%+ organically through 2030, North America keeps growing in the high teens, and the 2030 ~EUR 15bn ambition is reached largely organically (model: EUR 14.5bn by 2030). Operating leverage and mix take the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 26% (~22.5% adjusted operating margin), building markets recover as European and US rates ease, and the bolt-on engine keeps docking datacenter specialists at ROCE above WACC. Terminal growth 3%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The datacenter boom is a capex cycle, not a new base. Hyperscaler/colocation spending pauses in 2027-2028 and Legrand, a challenger to Vertiv and Schneider in white space, loses share as the incumbents bundle switchgear-to-chip offerings; datacenter sales fall ~15% in FY2027 while the building business stays in its 'slowdown' (management's own FY2025 word). Group growth is flat in FY2027 and reverts to the FY2015-2019 organic median of ~3%. Volume deleverage, pricing pressure and under-earning 2025-26 acquisitions compress the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 21.5% before a partial recovery to 22.5%. No solvency risk (A-, 1.9x net debt/EBITDA), so the bear is a de-rating and earnings reset, not distress. Terminal growth 2%, cap 15x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because 26% of sales and essentially all of the recent acceleration now rest on one end-market (AI/cloud datacenter capex) where Legrand is the challenger, not the incumbent, and because the building base was still in a slowdown in FY2025; there is no going-concern or covenant dimension, which is why it is not higher. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold for five years: sustained hyperscaler capex, a building-market recovery, and margin expansion above the range management itself guides to.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: owner FCF with SBC expensed (tiny here, 0.4% of revenue, so house and street nearly coincide), leases charged as an operating cost and excluded from net debt, risk carried in three probability-weighted scenario paths at a single EUR WACC, terminal value capped at an owner-FCF multiple a buyer plausibly pays for a moderately cyclical compounder, and no credit for acquisitions not yet paid for. The disagreement with the market is not about Legrand's quality but about how much of the datacenter acceleration is permanent and what multiple to pay for it after the stock has already de-rated from EUR 167 to EUR 124.
key_risks_to_valuation: Datacenter capex cycle: 26% of sales growing 25-30%; a hyperscaler spending pause is the single largest swing factor between bear and base
Balance-sheet anchors are from 31 Dec 2025; H1 2026 net debt is likely EUR 0.5-1.0bn higher after five 2026 acquisitions and the June dividend (~EUR 2-4/share)

Acquired growth is excluded from FY2028 onward; if Legrand keeps compounding bolt-ons at ROCE well above WACC the base understates value, if it overpays for datacenter assets at cycle peak the bear understates the damage
FX translation: 42% North/Central America and 20% RoW against EUR reporting; a 10% EUR move is ~6% of revenue
Terminal value is ~60% of base EV; the 18x cap binds in the base, so the value is sensitive to the cap and to WACC (see sensitivity grid)
OCEANE (EUR 800m, conversion EUR 159.03) adds 1.9% dilution if the stock re-rates above the conversion price
